hero_title: Cannabis explained with science, for people who want facts
hero_subtitle: Guides, data and sources on cannabis and cannabinoids: what the evidence says, what is still unknown and how to lower the risks.
mission_lead: We turn cannabis research into plain guides with sources you can check yourself.
mission_desc: High Doctor Foundation is an independent non-profit. We read the studies, keep the references and write down what they actually say, for patients, families and professionals. No products, no prescriptions, no miracle claims.
mission_li_1: Disseminate knowledge based on scientific evidence.
mission_li_2: Promote responsible use and harm reduction.
mission_li_3: Facilitate collaboration between researchers, doctors, patients, and organizations.
mission_li_4: Support research projects on medical cannabis.
mission_li_5: Create accessible educational resources for society.
vision_desc: To become a recognized European platform that connects people through culture, education, awareness and innovation. Building one of Europe's leading cannabis knowledge networks.
process_lead: Three steps, always in this order. Each one depends on the previous one.
process_step1_d: We read the primary literature, check who funded it and separate what is proven from what is still a hypothesis.
process_step2_d: We turn it into clear material, in the reader’s language and with the source in sight.
process_step3_d: We put researchers, clinicians and patients at the same table so that knowledge circulates.

evd_lead: Choose a topic. Each verdict uses the scale of the 2017 review by the US National Academies of Sciences, or the regulator's decision where there is one.
evd_disclaimer: Educational information, not medical advice. Talk to a health professional before starting or stopping any treatment.
evd_pain_f: Cannabis and cannabinoids reduce chronic pain in adults, with a modest effect in clinical trials.
evd_pain_m: It is one of the best-studied uses. The dose, the product and medical follow-up all matter.
evd_nausea_f: Oral cannabinoids are effective against the nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy.
evd_nausea_m: There are approved medicines for this use, although newer anti-nausea drugs are usually tried first.
evd_ms_f: Short-term oral cannabinoids improve the spasticity that patients themselves report.
evd_ms_m: In Spain a cannabinoid mouth spray (nabiximols) is approved for this use.
evd_epilepsy_f: Clinical trials show that CBD reduces seizures in Dravet and Lennox-Gastaut syndromes.
evd_epilepsy_m: The European Medicines Agency approved a CBD medicine for these syndromes in 2019. That does not extend to other epilepsies or to CBD sold in shops.
evd_sleep_f: Cannabinoids improve short-term sleep in people whose sleep is disturbed by pain, fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis or sleep apnoea.
evd_sleep_m: There is no good evidence for insomnia on its own, or for long-term use.
evd_anxiety_f: One small study found that CBD reduced anxiety during a public-speaking test in people with social anxiety.
evd_anxiety_m: That is not enough to recommend it. High doses of THC can also make anxiety worse.
evd_cancer_f: There is not enough evidence that cannabinoids treat cancer, gliomas included.
evd_cancer_m: Promises that cannabis cures cancer have no data behind them. Never give up a treatment because of one.
evd_psychosis_f: Cannabis use is associated with a higher risk of developing schizophrenia or other psychoses, highest in the most frequent users.
evd_psychosis_m: Frequency matters: daily use carries the greatest risk.
evd_driving_f: Cannabis use is associated with a higher risk of road traffic accidents.
evd_driving_m: It affects attention and reaction time. Do not drive after using cannabis.
evd_pregnancy_f: Smoking cannabis during pregnancy is associated with lower birth weight.
evd_pregnancy_m: Health authorities advise against cannabis during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

v2_hero_sub: Pick a topic and see how sure science really is, with the source so you can check it yourself.
v2_grade_legend: A: science is clear. E: there is not enough evidence.
v2_doc_a: This one is clear: many good studies agree.
v2_doc_b: Strong evidence, although there are nuances.
v2_doc_c: There are clues, but we need more studies.
v2_doc_d: Very little evidence so far. Be cautious.
v2_doc_e: There is no proof. Distrust anyone who promises otherwise.
v2_grid_lead: Open any topic to read what the studies found, what it means for you and the source.
v2_scale_lead: We use the evidence scale of the 2017 review by the US National Academies of Sciences, or the regulator's decision where there is one. The grade says how sure science is, not whether something is good or bad.
v2_def_b: Substantial: strong evidence with few doubts.
v2_def_c: Moderate: good studies, but not enough to be sure.
v2_def_d: Limited: a few small or weak studies.
